items.title: 'Trump Needs a Way Out of This War': Michel Yakovleff explains 'charade' over US-Iran negotiations
items.summary:
Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome General Michel Yakovleff, Professor at Sciences-Po and Former Vice-Chief of Staff at NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe (Shape).. He presents a strategic rather than tactical reading of the current lull in the US-Iran conflict. He argues that the apparent de-escalation is not evidence of diplomatic progress but of mounting structural constraints. Rather than viewing pauses in hostilities as signs of imminent peace, he frames them as consequences of political pressure, military logistics and industrial limitations.
 
At the centre of his argument is the proposition that modern warfare is ultimately governed by sustainability. Missile stockpiles, industrial production capacity, domestic political legitimacy and alliance commitments become as decisive as battlefield success. General Yakovleff contends that the United States retains ample military capability to continue operations against Iran in isolation, yet doing so progressively erodes its ability to deter other adversaries, reassure allies and sustain global commitments.

items.title: IRGC says missiles destroyed three US F-35 jets at Jordan base
items.summary: IRGC says missiles destroyed three US F-35 jets at Jordan base Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says it fired several ballistic missiles at Jordan’s al-Azraq airbase, which hosts US F-35 fighter jets. The IRGC said the attack targeted a runway and maintenance hangar in response to a US strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island that killed two parents and their child, the Fars news agency reported. It said the missiles completely destroyed three F-35 aircraft and inflicted “heavy damage” on three others. The IRGC also said the attack killed several officers and members of the base’s technical and maintenance teams. “A number of enemy officers and technical and maintenance personnel were also killed in this attack. Our region is no place for the infanticidal army that cruelly slaughters innocent families in the middle of the night while they sleep,” it said. The group said its struggle, alongside Jordan’s, would continue until “the last American occupier is expelled from the Islamic lands”.

items.title: US awards Lockheed Martin $58.6bn Patriot missile contract
items.summary: US awards Lockheed Martin $58.6bn Patriot missile contract The US Army has awarded Lockheed Martin a contract worth up to $58.6bn to expand production of Patriot interceptor missiles, the Reuters news agency reported. The seven-year agreement will run from the 2026 financial year until 2032 as Washington seeks to rebuild weapons stockpiles depleted by its war on Iran and military support for Ukraine. The deal replaces a one-year contract worth $4.7bn that the army issued in April. It establishes a long-term procurement programme for PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement interceptors, which target aircraft and ballistic and cruise missiles.

items.title: Trump hails late US Senator Lindsey Graham as 'true American original'
items.summary: Trump hails late US Senator Lindsey Graham as 'true American original' World leaders gathered in Washington, DC, on Tuesday for the funeral ceremony for late Republican US Senator Lindsey Graham, who was instrumental in advocating for the war on Iran and a staunch supporter of Israel. Among those attending were Ukrainian President Zelensky and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu. Delivering remarks at the ceremony, Trump called Graham a "beloved friend" and "a true American original". "He never saw a war that he didn’t like," Trump said, drawing laughter before adding that Graham supported military power "for the good of our country." "Above all, Lindsey Graham believed in a strong America," Trump said. "He had unwavering faith in the righteousness of American power." US President Donald Trump delivers remarks during the funeral service for the late US Senator Lindsey Graham at the Washington National Cathedral, on 28 July 2026 (AFP)

items.title: Tehran says it will halt strikes after Washington pauses attacks
items.summary: Tehran says it will halt strikes after Washington pauses attacks Tehran has said it will stop retaliatory attacks on neighbouring Gulf countries following a two-night pause on US strikes targeting Iran. "Our strategy has essentially been retaliatory, we have also halted our retaliatory operations,” Iran’s army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said, according to the AFP news agency. The US has not attacked Iran for two consecutive nights, following daily strikes since fighting between the two countries resumed two weeks ago. Tehran has not launched any attacks on US-allied states so far on Sunday.

items.title: US passes $1 trillion military spending bill
items.summary: US passes $1 trillion military spending bill The US House of Representatives narrowly passed its version of a massive defence policy bill on Wednesday, despite Democrats' concerns about its huge price tag, the Iran war and a provision that would boost Pentagon ties to Israel. The fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act, or NDAA, authorises an unprecedented $1.15 trillion in military spending and passed the House by a vote of 216 to 212. The vote was largely along party lines, as all but seven Republicans voted in favour of the measure and all but six Democrats voted against. The NDAA has come under fire for a provision aimed at increasing military technology cooperation with Israel, despite growing support among voters for halting military assistance to Israel. The bill's future in the Senate is now uncertain as Democrats objected to the substantial funding allocated to the Pentagon at a time when President Donald Trump and his fellow Republicans are slashing spending on social programmes. clusters.headline: Most Americans say Iran war isn't worth fighting

items.title: Most Americans say Iran war isn't worth fighting
Support for Israeli-US war on Iran falls as most Americans call it pointless
items.summary: Support for Israeli-US war on Iran falls as most Americans call it pointless Public backing in the United States for the war on Iran has continued to weaken, a new poll has found. About two-thirds of US adults said the conflict which Israel pushed the country in to had no purpose and was not worth pursuing, the survey by the Associated Press and the NORC Center for Public Affairs Research showed. The findings also indicated declining support for President Donald Trump’s decision to wage war, with few respondents favouring a prolonged conflict. Only two in 10 adults supported continuing US military operations against Iran. Three in 10 said Washington should halt its attacks and pursue another ceasefire through negotiations. The results point to growing public opposition as the war continues to drain US military resources, increase fuel costs, and destabilise the wider Middle East.

items.title: Egypt says drone attack sparked fire on American LNG ships
items.summary: Egypt says drone attack sparked fire on American LNG ships Egypt has attributed a fire that damaged two vessels at the Mediterranean port of Damietta to a drone attack, marking its first official account of Wednesday’s incident. The Egyptian cabinet said preliminary findings showed that a drone caused the 29 July blaze. No group has taken responsibility. Authorities have opened an investigation into the circumstances of the attack, citing the need to defend Egypt’s national security and interests. Maritime security company Ambrey said the drone struck a US-owned floating gas storage tanker before flames spread to a second vessel. Officials reported no casualties. Egypt’s Petroleum Ministry had previously confirmed the fire but did not identify its cause. The attack has raised fears that the regional war could spread further after Iran targeted US-linked interests in several countries. If confirmed as part of the wider conflict, it would represent the first attack of its kind on Egyptian territory since the war began.

items.title: Trouble in Paris? There's a Gaullist cure for that American hubris
items.summary: Last month, as world leaders prepared to gather in France for the G7 Summit, French officials had Donald Trump on the mind. Using its privileges as host, Paris worked diligently to avoid any hiccups that might upset the U.S. president. First, it delayed the meeting from June 14 to June 16, ensuring that it wouldn’t interfere with Trump’s 80th birthday celebration, or the cage match on the White House lawn that accompanied it. Then, French President Emmanuel Macron went “out of his way” to design an agenda to “appeal to the sort of things Trump wants,” as one analyst told Reuters. Last, and perhaps most bizarrely, French officials delayed the ceremonial transfer of the remains of French Resistance hero Marc Bloch, who was set to be reinterred at France’s illustrious Panthéon in the heart of Paris on June 16. items.title: Will naming, shaming & sanctioning terror in Sudan stop bloodshed?
items.summary: In June, a bipartisan group of senators introduced the Preventing External Aggression and Conflict Escalation (PEACE) in Sudan Act of 2026. In the House, the pending U.S. Engagement in Sudanese Peace Act and the RSF Terrorism Designation Act partly overlap with the PEACE Act. One of the most consequential questions raised by the various bills is whether to designate Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary force that has been at war with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) since 2023, as a terrorist group. What effects could a terrorist designation for the RSF have? Would a designation make ceasefire negotiations – being pursued, although amid much criticism, by President Donald Trump’s Africa advisor Massad Boulos – easier or more difficult? And would a designation constrain the United Arab Emirates (UAE), which is credibly accused of backing the RSF? clusters.headline: Party elites so blind they can't see their base turning against the war

items.title: Party elites so blind they can't see their base turning against the war
items.summary: Last week, only four House Republicans voted with 210 Democrats to pass a war powers resolution to end the U.S. war with Iran. That means 208 House Republicans voted to continue the war. Hours later, the Republican-led Senate killed the measure, with only one GOP senator voting with the Democrats to end the war, de facto joining four other Republicans who were either absent or missed the vote. The overwhelming majority of congressional Republicans are still clearly committed to President Donald Trump’s war. Republican voters? Not so much. items.summary: Iran holds funeral for pilot killed during March mission Funeral ceremonies have begun in Iran for air force pilot Majid Kazemi, who was killed during a combat mission in March. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei paid tribute to the second brigadier general after authorities recovered and identified his remains. Kazemi was one of four crew members aboard two Islamic Republic of Iran Air Force Su-24 bombers taking part in an attack on 2 March 2026. Iranian military officials said air defence systems struck the aircraft while they were flying over the Gulf. Baghaei said search operations and identification efforts remained under way for the other three crew members. He announced the funeral processions in a statement on X as mourners gathered to honour Kazemi.

clusters.headline: IRGC says it downed hostile drone over southwestern Iran

items.title: IRGC says it downed hostile drone over southwestern Iran
items.summary: IRGC says it downed hostile drone over southwestern Iran Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says it intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone over the southwestern port city of Bandar Imam Khomeini early on Thursday. The IRGC’s local division detected the unmanned aircraft inside the city’s airspace before shooting it down, the Tasnim news agency reported. Parts of the drone fell onto a residential property following the interception, but authorities reported no deaths. An IRGC explosives team later secured the wreckage, removed it from the house and neutralised any remaining danger, Tasnim said. The military did not identify the drone’s type, origin or intended target. Bandar Imam Khomeini sits on the Gulf coast in Iran’s Khuzestan province and contains one of the country’s most important commercial ports.

items.summary: Iran blames US for Hormuz closure as Oman talks continue Iran says negotiations with Oman remain under way in Tehran as efforts continue to address the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and disruption to global shipping. Foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Iranian and Omani officials had held several rounds of discussions since talks began last week, including further meetings on Thursday. Baghaei blamed US and Israeli military operations for destabilising the vital waterway. “What is clear is that currently, the Strait of Hormuz is closed due to American actions and the insecurity that America has imposed on this waterway,” Baghaei told the ILNA news agency. “International shipping is being harmed and damaged solely because of American actions.”

clusters.headline: Trump's Lebanon fantasy is running smack into reality

items.title: Trump's Lebanon fantasy is running smack into reality
items.summary: On June 26, two official delegations — one from Israel and one from Lebanon — signed a framework agreement with great fanfare in Washington. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, openly enthusiastic, framed the event as paving the way toward “lasting peace and security” between Beirut and Tel Aviv. A month later, President Donald Trump received Lebanese President Joseph Aoun at the White House. Once again, Rubio welcomed the visit and reiterated the goal of disarming Hezbollah and achieving a complete and definitive peace between Lebanon and its southern neighbor. Like Tel Aviv, Rubio favors a top-down approach that centers on force and coercion. To neutralize both Tehran and Hezbollah, this camp hopes to combine strong military action against Iranian territory with maximum pressure on the government in Beirut. The goal is two-fold: to strong-arm the Lebanese government into sidelining Hezbollah and to permanently separate the Lebanese and Iranian equations. Within the Trump administration, not everyone is convinced that this roadmap is the most effective approach. Vice President JD Vance

items.summary: Israel is spending wads of cash on public diplomacy in a desperate attempt to reverse waning American support for the country after it stands accused of genocide in Gaza and pushing the U.S. into the Iran war. Since Oct. 7, Israel has spent over a billion dollars on global “hasbara” — television appearances, social media campaigns, chat-bot training, and other efforts to influence how people think about Israel. And this “public diplomacy” budget more than quadrupled in the last year alone. items.title: Climate Change Archives - Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
items.summary: In 1978, the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists published a cover story titled “Is mankind warming the Earth?” The answer then, as now, was an “unqualified ‘yes.’” Between July 2023 and June 2024, the average global temperature was over 1.5 degrees Celsius (or 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warmer than the pre-industrial average, the result of over a century of rampant fossil fuel use and associated greenhouse gas emissions. This warming has resulted in global climate change. The Bulletin covers all aspects of the causes and wide-ranging impacts of this existential crisis, from glacier retreat and sea level rise to drought, extreme weather, and intense wildfires. We also investigate the most promising ways to slow and eventually halt global warming, probing uncertainties and irreversible tipping points in the Earth’s climate and biosphere that threatens all life on Earth.

items.title: Biosecurity Archives - Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
items.summary: As part of its coverage of disruptive technologies that might come to pose global-scale threats, the Bulletin publishes articles on all the ways in which emerging science and technology can affect biological risks. COVID-19 highlighted those risks and led to voluminous coverage of the pandemic and related subjects, including gain-of-function research that could create potentially dangerous new pathogens that might, if accidentally released, spark a disease outbreak. But we also attempt to answer a wide variety of biosecurity- and biosafety-related questions: Are the laboratories used to study pathogens as safe and secure as they need to be? Will artificial intelligence make it easier and simpler for bad actors to develop or use biological weapons? Will efforts at human enhancement spark arms races or exacerbate societal inequality? Do policies that reduce compulsory vaccination increase the threat of diseases once thought tamed? Can political disinformation about bioweapons disrupt international efforts to minimize threats?

items.summary: Al-Sadr tells Iran-backed groups to keep Iraq out of war Influential Iraqi cleric Muqtada al-Sadr has urged Iran’s Revolutionary Guard and allied armed groups to stop launching attacks from Iraq. Al-Sadr warned the groups against pulling the country into another conflict and called on Baghdad to assert state control. “Rogue militias must not give our brothers in the Gulf states a pretext to target our sacred land,” he wrote on X. He urged all sides not to “be drawn into the schemes of the Zionist-American enemy to incite brothers to fight and kill one another”. “Iraq and its people need peace,” al-Sadr said, calling for a region free from foreign military bases and colonial domination.

items.summary: Biologists say cargo ships stranded in Gulf may carry highly potent invasive species around the world as trade resumes The closure of the strait of Hormuz has created conditions for an extreme global biodiversity threat, with scientists warning that thousands of stranded ships could spread invasive marine species across the world’s oceans once they begin sailing again. More than 1,500 commercial vessels have been stuck in the Gulf since the strategic waterway closed on 28 February after the outbreak of the US-Israel war on Iran . An international team of marine biologists said that with the stranded ships remaining motionless, their hulls were becoming encrusted with marine life – from microbes and algae to barnacles and other invertebrates – that could hitchhike to ports around the world when trade resumed. items.summary: Tehran has not been bombed into submission, leaving America unable to enforce its demands without a ground war that it does not want Has Iran won a war it didn’t start against the United States? clusters.headline: Iran valt Jordanië aan, VS en Saudi-Arabië bombarderen milities in Irak

items.title: Iran valt Jordanië aan, VS en Saudi-Arabië bombarderen milities in Irak
items.summary: Iran heeft gisteravond en vanochtend raketaanvallen uitgevoerd op Jordanië. De Jordaanse staatsnieuwszender meldt dat het leger vijf raketten heeft "onderschept en vernietigd". Ook een Amerikaanse legerbasis in Jordanië werd aangevallen. De VS spreekt van een verrassingsaanval en stelt dat alle ballistische raketten zijn onderschept. De Iraanse aanval heeft het einde ingeluid van een gevechtspauze die zeker vier dagen heeft geduurd. In Irak zijn afgelopen nacht bombardementen uitgevoerd. Het Amerikaanse leger heeft daar samen met de strijdkrachten van Saudi-Arabië pro-Iraanse milities aangevallen, zo hebben de twee bondgenoten bekendgemaakt. Het Saudische ministerie van Defensie zegt dat deze aanvallen een vergelding zijn voor droneaanvallen op Saudische energiecentrales van de afgelopen dagen. In de verklaringen van de Amerikaanse en Saudische autoriteiten staat niet vermeld of er een direct verband is met de Iraanse raketaanval op Jordanië, die kort daarvoor werd gemeld. items.summary: Iran proposes temporary Hormuz plan to give itself more control over transit Iran has proposed to Oman a temporary arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, under which one direction of traffic and part of the traffic in the opposite direction would pass through Iranian waters, allowing for greater Iranian control of transit. Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi told state TV on Tuesday that Tehran rejected an Omani proposal for an equal division of transit routes between the two countries, saying that it did not address Iran’s security concerns amid ongoing US-Israeli attacks on the country. He said that if Muscat rejected Iran’s proposal, the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed, adding that Tehran had never recognised the alternative southern route along Oman’s coast.

While prices are still well below previous wartime peaks, oil markets are once again under pressure—and things are almost certain to get worse. During the first round of the war, oil prices never reached the calamitous levels predicted by some analysts. This seems to have taught the White House a flawed lesson: that the global oil system is more robust than the doomsayers claim and that a war over the world’s most important energy chokepoint can be fought without a significant energy crisis at home. items.title: Trump is playing chicken with America's oil reserves
items.summary: Back in 1975, reeling from the Arab Oil Embargo of 1973, President Gerald Ford signed the Energy Policy and Conservation Act. The law established the nation’s Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) and framed it as a rainy day fund, made ready for the benefit of the American people should a crisis in supply reach us once more. Today, after two consecutive administrations, our rainy day fund has been drawn down to the lowest levels since 1983 . Biden drew down 50 million barrels in response to COVID. The next year, he withdrew an additional 180 million barrels in response to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, the largest release in SPR history, arguing that the move was needed to calm gasoline prices and cushion the shock from the war. Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration (July 2026) Now, President Donald Trump is draining what is left to manage the price and supply shocks of his Iran war. The poll found that 69 percent of Americans, including four in 10 Republicans, think Trump has not "clearly explained the goals of US military involvement in Iran." Approval of the conflict has been below 40 percent since the US and Israel launched strikes on 28 February - a stark contrast to the opening months of other recent conflicts. If the United States conditions a civilian nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia on the kingdom's immediate accession to the Abraham Accords , it would be collapsing two fundamentally different policy objectives into a single diplomatic test. clusters.headline: La «situation explosive» en Cisjordanie occupée est «une manière pour Netanyahu de reprendre la main»

items.title: La «situation explosive» en Cisjordanie occupée est «une manière pour Netanyahu de reprendre la main»
items.summary: La Cisjordanie occupée a connu un nouveau week-end de violences après des affrontements meurtriers entre Palestiniens et colons israéliens, vendredi 24 juillet, dans la localité de Tell. Ces violences continueront de s'aggraver sans action forte du gouvernement israélien. Et cela n'a rien d'anodin à quelques semaines des élections législatives anticipées, que Benyamin Netanyahu espère bien remporter. La violence des colons a fortement augmenté depuis l'entrée en fonction du gouvernement israélien actuel, avec une reprise particulièrement marquée en mars et avril 2026, pendant la guerre entre les États-Unis, Israël et l'Iran. L'analyse de Denis Charbit, professeur de science politique à l'université ouverte d'Israël, dont le dernier ouvrage, Yitzhak Rabin, la paix assassinée ? Une mémoire morcelée, a été publié aux éditions JC Lattès.

items.title: Disruptive Technologies Archives - Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
items.summary: The Bulletin’s disruptive technology vertical tracks a wide variety of scientific and technological advances that could—either in the present or the future—pose an existential threat to humanity. These technology areas include biosecurity and biological threats more generally; generative artificial intelligence and its deployment in various industries; autonomous weapons; digitized surveillance systems; and cyber-enabled information warfare that can pollute, and cause chaos in, the world’s information ecosystem. How can humans attempt to roll out new technologies responsibly, benefitting the greater good without destroying civilization in the process? This space is dedicated to answering that question in all its ethical dimensions.

items.title: Nuclear Risk Archives - Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
items.summary: Founded by scientists and engineers of the Manhattan Project in the wake of the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists has been alerting humanity to the danger of nuclear catastrophe since December 1945. For 80 years, the Bulletin has relentlessly pursued this mission by informing the public, policymakers, and scientists about new and evolving risks from nuclear technologies. Our authors include the world’s leading experts in the fields of nuclear weapons and their delivery platforms, nuclear security, nuclear safety, and nuclear waste policy. These experts and a staff of editors work together to provide accessible, authoritative articles for policy makers and citizens alike, with the aim of ensuring that nuclear science makes life on Earth better, not worse.

Beijing accused him of spying. The Tatmadaw, or military, seized power in 1962 and has ruled the country in varying iterations ever since. clusters.headline: From the strait of Hormuz to the North Sea, a global maritime war rages around us – and more than the price of oil is at stake | Simon Tisdall

items.title: From the strait of Hormuz to the North Sea, a global maritime war rages around us – and more than the price of oil is at stake | Simon Tisdall
items.summary: The collapse of the rules-based order is not confined to the land: we’re imperilled as centuries of maritime cooperation sink beneath the waves The US military campaign to protect merchant shipping from Iranian attacks by asserting direct maritime control in the strait of Hormuz is not an idea unique to Donald Trump’s administration. Almost exactly 200 years ago, in the period 1825-27, a powerful US naval squadron led by Commodore John Rodgers was sent to the Mediterranean to defend American ships from the depredations of Greek corsairs and pirates. For all the new-minted republic’s brave talk of liberty, the US squadron did not assist Greece’s ongoing “regime change” struggle for independence from the Ottoman empire. Its sole, self-serving purpose was to defend US trade, markets and business interests. After abandoning his call for a people’s revolution in Tehran , this, too, is what Trump’s reckless war with Iran has now boiled down to. Simon Tisdall is a Guardian foreign affairs commentator Continue reading...

clusters.headline: NYT: Trump wisselde plots van regeringsvliegtuig vanwege Iraanse dreiging

items.title: NYT: Trump wisselde plots van regeringsvliegtuig vanwege Iraanse dreiging
items.summary: "Een reële dreiging" door partijen met banden met Iran was de reden dat de Amerikaanse president Trump deze maand abrupt van vliegtuig wisselde. Dat schrijft de krant The New York Times (NYT) op basis van anonieme bronnen. De wissel vond plaats na de NAVO-top in de Turkse hoofdstad Ankara. Trump vloog daarheen met de Boeing 747-8 die hij van de regering van Qatar cadeau had gekregen. De Amerikaanse veiligheidsdienst Secret Service drong er volgens de NYT bij Trump op aan om van toestel te wisselen. Dat zou gebeuren uit "veiligheidsoverwegingen". Het luxe regeringsvliegtuig heeft minder geavanceerde veiligheidssystemen dan de twee oudere Air Force One-toestellen. Zo mist het toestel cruciale verdedigingssystemen, zoals anti-raketapparatuur. Gemunt op Trump Volgens de anonieme Amerikaanse functionarissen was de dreiging van de pro-Iraanse actoren niet gericht op het nieuwe regeringsvliegtuig, maar hadden ze het gemunt op Trump zelf, ongeacht het toestel waarmee hij op dat moment vloog. Details over de dreiging werden volgens de NYT niet breed binnen de regering gedeeld. Belangrijke led

items.title: Iran's IRGC says four vessels stopped in Hormuz in last 24 hours
items.summary: Iran's IRGC says four vessels stopped in Hormuz in last 24 hours Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) naval forces have barred four ships from crossing the Strait of Hormuz in the last 24 hours, Iranian state television reports. According to the report, the ships were stopped after warning shots were fired. They were attempting to cross via the strait's southern corridor - which the IRGC has declared an "unsafe passage". The group has warned that any vessels trying to navigate "unsafe routes" through the contested waterway will be met with a "forceful response".

items.summary: In delen van Nederland was rond 22.30 uur een vuurbal aan de hemel te zien. Onder meer vanuit Amsterdam, Utrecht, Almere, Dronten, Arnhem en het Friese Gaastmeer kwamen berichten van mensen die het bijzondere fenomeen in de avondschemering zagen. Volgens satellietdeskundige Marco Langbroek van de TU Delft gaat het om een satelliet van Elon Musks SpaceX die terugkeerde in de atmosfeer, Starlink 1541. "Hij kwam boven Engeland de atmosfeer binnen en begon daar op te breken en op te branden. Dat gebeurt doorgaans op hoogtes tussen de 90 en 50 kilometer." Bekijk hier de beelden van de vuurbal: Langbroek zag hem zelf bij Texel over komen. "De re-entry was wel voor deze nacht verwacht, maar omdat er een onzekerheid van vier uur was, was moeilijk te voorspellen wanneer precies. Ik zat zelf met enkele mensen op het dek van een zeilschip toen we het zagen, geheel bij toeval." "Er was ook nog minutenlang een dampspoor in de atmosfeer te zien. items.title: Nederland geeft deel strategische oliereserve vrij
items.summary: Nederland is begonnen met het op de markt brengen van een deel van de strategische oliereserve. Dat moet de omhooggeschoten olieprijs drukken. Het gaat om 2,7 miljoen vaten van commerciële partijen. De komende weken volgt mogelijk ook een deel van de voorraad van de Staat. In maart kondigde het Internationaal Energieagentschap (IEA) aan 400 miljoen vaten uit de noodreserves van de aangesloten landen vrij te geven. Het was de grootste gezamenlijke vrijgave door de IEA-lidstaten ooit. Niet alle reserves komen in een keer op de markt. Het gaat gecoördineerd en verspreid over een aantal maanden. Tot nu toe waren de Nederlandse reserves niet nodig, maar door de oplopende olieprijs is er nu wel behoefte aan. Prijsdempend effect Het IEA bestaat vooral uit ontwikkelde landen die voor hun economie afhankelijk zijn van olie. Lidstaten zijn verplicht een oliereserve aan te houden die gelijkstaat aan circa drie maanden aan import. items.title: 'Nobel' de matemáticas por resolver la conjetura de Kakeya, un endiablado juego de agujas
items.summary: La pregunta parece un acertijo para pasar la tarde: ¿cuánto espacio se necesita para girar una aguja de manera que llegue a apuntar en todas las direcciones? No se engañe, el problema es fácil de formular, pero extraordinariamente difícil de resolver. Se llama desafío de Kakeya y ha permanecido más de un siglo sin respuesta hasta que, en 2025, una joven matemática china, Hong Wang , de solo 34 años, logró destejer el enredo para tres dimensiones. Su solución, que se extiende a lo largo de más de un centenar de páginas, ha merecido este jueves la medalla Fields, el premio más prestigioso de las matemáticas, junto a los trabajos del también chino Yu Deng, el estadounidense John Pardon y el canadiense Jacob Tsimerman. Los Fields son considerados los 'Nobel' de las matemáticas. La Unión Matemática Internacional (ICM) los otorga cada cuatro años a talentos que no han cumplido los 40 en el marco de un congreso internacional que en esta ocasión se celebra en Filadelfia (EE.UU.). items.summary: For decades, Iran has sought to diminish America’s military presence and political influence in the Middle East. Yet some ambitions carry within them the seeds of their own undoing. The very policies intended to push out the United States have instead strengthened the rationale for Washington’s continued engagement. Before the erosion of its regional axis, Iran based its security doctrine on forward defense, projecting influence beyond its borders to keep threats at bay. However, what Tehran regarded as a defensive strategy , the Persian Gulf states perceived as an expansionist bid for regional primacy. As a result, they deepened their security ties with Washington, making the U.S. military presence more indispensable to Gulf security rather than less. Iran’s current approach suggests that it is repeating the same strategic mistake, both in its confrontation with the United States and in its vision for the regional order that will follow. items.summary: Public opinion on Israel is shifting rapidly , but there was little evidence of that at a House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing Wednesday. The Middle East and North Africa Subcommittee's discussion of "The Next Phase of the Abraham Accords" largely reflected a Washington consensus on Israel that is quickly losing support. The discussion was ostensibly focused on expanding the agreements, signed during President Donald Trump’s first term, that normalized relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, and Morocco. But the conversation quickly expanded to broader questions of the U.S.-Israel and Israel-Palestine relationship. In particular, lawmakers and witnesses explored whether the pursuit of a Palestinian state was a necessary step to further the accords and bring in Saudi Arabia, which has previously said they would not sign the accords without a pathway to statehood. items.summary: US House of Representatives votes to halt Iran war, in another symbolic rebuke of Trump The Republican-led US House of Representatives backed legislation on Thursday directing President Donald Trump to halt the US war on Iran, the latest symbolic rebuke of the Republican president from Congress. The vote was 214-208 in favour of the war powers resolution as four Republicans joined Democrats in voting for it. The resolution, introduced by Representative Pramila Jayapal, a Washington Democrat, directs Trump "to remove the use of United States Armed Forces from hostilities" against Iran unless Congress authorises it. However, it was largely symbolic. Lawmakers have passed similar resolutions repeatedly in recent months, but they have not led to the cessation of war.

Plus letters from Blaine Stothard and Harvey Gilbert Simon Tisdall’s article ( Trump, not Iran, is the world’s greatest danger. He’s a one-man weapon of mass destruction, 18 July ) is a forceful polemic, but it risks turning a structural problem into a personal one. If Donald Trump is uniquely reckless, that deserves criticism. items.summary: How Israel's dream of being the Middle East's trade hub is unravelling Submitted by Ahmed Alqarout on Wed, 07/22/2026 - 15:45 Gulf powers are working out new corridors that would bypass the need to engage with Tel Aviv A ship docks at the Emirati port of Jebel Ali on 18 June 2020 (Karim Sahib/AFP) On The India -Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) has died at its Israeli end. Gulf states and their allies are now racing to build rival lines. In June, the Saudi and Turkish transport ministers signed memoranda to revive the Ottoman-era Hejaz railway as a corridor connecting their nations via Jordan and Syria - routed deliberately around Israel. And the UAE has opened talks on a trade route from the Syrian coast through Iraq to its own Gulf ports. clusters.headline: Houthi's beschieten olietankers, opnieuw Amerikaans bombardement op Iran

items.title: Houthi's beschieten olietankers, opnieuw Amerikaans bombardement op Iran
items.summary: De Houthi-rebellen in Jemen zeggen dat ze met luchtaanvallen twee Saudische olietankers in de Rode Zee hebben geraakt. De tankers zouden de zeeblokkade van de rebellengroep hebben geschonden. Volgens het Saudische persbureau SPA is in elk geval een schip geraakt toen het op de Rode Zee voer. Er brak brand uit op de boeg, maar alle bemanningsleden konden in veiligheid worden gebracht. Zeeblokkade Maandag kondigden de Houthi's per direct een zeeblokkade af tegen Saudi-Arabië , de aartsvijand van hun bondgenoot Iran. De blokkade heeft betrekking op het verkeer door de zeestraat Bab el-Mandeb, tussen Jemen en de Hoorn van Afrika. De zeestraat is net als de Straat van Hormuz belangrijk voor de olie-export en dreigt een nieuw brandpunt te worden in het conflict in de regio. Het is nog onduidelijk welke gevolgen de aangekondigde maritieme blokkade heeft voor de internationale scheepvaart in het gebied. Tijdens de oorlog in Gaza vielen de Houthi's maandenlang schepen aan in en rond de Rode Zee. Gisteren wijzigden vijf tankers hun koers in de Rode Zee om de zeestraat Bab el-Mandeb te mijden.

items.title: Unesco zet gebombardeerde Libanese stad Tyrus op lijst van bedreigd erfgoed
items.summary: De duizenden jaren oude stad Tyrus in Libanon komt op een lijst voor bedreigd werelderfgoed te staan. Dat heeft VN-organisatie Unesco besloten volgens het Franse persbureau AFP. Het Israëlische leger heeft de Libanese havenstad in de oorlog met Hezbollah herhaaldelijk gebombardeerd. De Libanese regering heeft Israël ervan beschuldigd dat het onder meer een Romeinse zuil in het oude centrum van Tyrus heeft getroffen. Unesco heeft op verzoek van Libanon nu een extra beschermde status toegekend aan Tyrus, dat sinds 1984 op de lijst van werelderfgoed staat. "De locatie is geraakt en heeft schade opgelopen", wordt Unesco door AFP geciteerd. De VN-organisatie maakt zich ook zorgen over het onderhoud van de ruïnes. "Er is geen sprake meer van optimale omstandigheden om de unieke universele waarde van de locatie te beschermen." Israëlisch evacuatiebevel Een groot deel van de inwoners van Tyrus is de stad ontvlucht. In de strijd met Hezbollah had Israël bewoners opgedragen de havenstad te verlaten. items.title: Yémen: les Houthis revendiquent des frappes contre «deux pétroliers saoudiens» en mer Rouge
items.summary: Les Houthis ont revendiqué des frappes contre deux pétroliers en mer Rouge. L'agence maritime britannique a annoncé qu'un pétrolier avait été touché mercredi 22 juillet par un projectile dans la mer Rouge au large de l'Arabie saoudite. Les rebelles Houthis pro-iraniens avaient adressé des avertissements radio à des navires après l'annonce lundi 20 juillet d'un blocus maritime de l'Arabie saoudite. Des données analysées mercredi 22 juillet montrent qu'au moins neuf bateaux avaient fait demi-tour au large du Yémen, dans les environs du détroit de Bab el-Mandeb ou en mer Rouge.

items.title: Gasprijs stijgt na oplaaiende geweld in Midden-Oosten
items.summary: De gasprijs is de afgelopen tijd flink gestegen. Op de Europese groothandelsmarkt kwam de prijs vandaag uit op ruim 62 euro per megawattuur. Minder dan een maand geleden was die nog onder de 41 euro. De gasprijs is nu ook net iets hoger dan de eerdere piek in maart tijdens het begin van de oorlog tussen Amerika en Iran. Voor die oorlog, die eind februari begon, was de prijs minder dan 30 euro. Daarmee is de gasprijs nu dus meer dan verdubbeld. Qatar, het land aan de Perzische Golf, is een belangrijke exporteur van gas. Maar door de vijandigheden rond de Straat van Hormuz is de export van dat gas nu moeilijker. Ook zijn er tijdens de oorlog gasinstallaties in Qatar geraakt. Dynamisch contract Vooral mensen met een dynamisch energiecontract merken de stijging van de gasprijs snel. Met zo'n contract wordt de gasprijs dagelijks aangepast op basis van de groothandelsprijs. Bij bijvoorbeeld ANWB Energie is die vandaag 1,49 euro per kubieke meter. Voordat de oorlog begon was dat 1,15 euro. Voor mensen met een dynamisch contract stijgt de prijs dus wel minder hard dan de groothandelsprijs. D

clusters.headline: Iraanse fotograaf laat zien dat 'Hormuz' meer is dan oorlog

items.title: Iraanse fotograaf laat zien dat 'Hormuz' meer is dan oorlog
items.summary: Al bijna twee weken worden de bombardementen op Iran alsmaar heviger. Niet alleen militaire doelen, ook doelen die burgers gebruiken worden steeds meer geraakt. Zo zijn rondom de zuidelijke havenstad Bandar Abbas tunnels, bruggen en communicatie-infrastructuur gebombardeerd. Dat heeft natuurlijk impact op de bevolking. Want waar de oorlog en de Straat van Hormuz voor veel mensen een nieuwskop zijn, is het gebied ook een thuis voor miljoenen Iraniërs. De Iraanse fotograaf Morteza Niknahad (42) portretteert al jaren de mensen uit zijn omgeving. Hij geeft met zijn werk een uniek inkijkje in het leven van de inwoners van het gebied die we nauwelijks te horen of te zien krijgen. "Het geluid van explosies is er constant. We blijven hele nachten wakker om het nieuws te volgen", vertelt Niknahad in een spraakbericht. De fotograaf, geboren en getogen in de zuidelijke havenstad Bandar Abbas, maakt al jaren foto's van het gebied rond de Straat van Hormuz. items.title: The US war on Iran is spinning out of control | Mohamad Bazzi
items.summary: Trump’s conflict keeps escalating, with Saudi Arabia joining airstrikes in Iraq and reportedly planning an attack on the Houthis. A recession could follow The US war against Iran is spiraling out of control. Over the past week, the conflict has expanded across the Middle East , with attacks and counterattacks in at least five other countries. Instead of a quick war that sought to topple Iran’s regime, Donald Trump has started a regional conflict that risks severely disrupting energy supplies and prices – and triggering a global recession. After a few days of relative calm, the conflict resumed with the Pentagon carrying out almost nightly strikes against Iran, and Tehran retaliating against US military bases in the region. The conflict also extended to attacks in Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Yemen, Jordan and Egypt. And there’s little sign that peace negotiations between the US and Iran, which are being brokered by Pakistan and Qatar, are making much progress. Continue reading...

Using its privileges as host, Paris worked diligently to avoid any hiccups that might upset the U.S. president. First, it delayed the meeting from June 14 to June 16, ensuring that it wouldn’t interfere with Trump’s 80th birthday celebration, or the cage match on the White House lawn that accompanied it. That means 208 House Republicans voted to continue the war. Hours later, the Republican-led Senate killed the measure, with only one GOP senator voting with the Democrats to end the war, de facto joining four other Republicans who were either absent or missed the vote. items.title: Iran holds funeral for pilot killed during March mission
items.summary: Iran holds funeral for pilot killed during March mission Funeral ceremonies have begun in Iran for air force pilot Majid Kazemi, who was killed during a combat mission in March. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei paid tribute to the second brigadier general after authorities recovered and identified his remains. Kazemi was one of four crew members aboard two Islamic Republic of Iran Air Force Su-24 bombers taking part in an attack on 2 March 2026. Iranian military officials said air defence systems struck the aircraft while they were flying over the Gulf. Baghaei said search operations and identification efforts remained under way for the other three crew members. He announced the funeral processions in a statement on X as mourners gathered to honour Kazemi.

items.title: Support for Israeli-US war on Iran falls as most Americans call it pointless
items.summary: Support for Israeli-US war on Iran falls as most Americans call it pointless Public backing in the United States for the war on Iran has continued to weaken, a new poll has found. About two-thirds of US adults said the conflict which Israel pushed the country in to had no purpose and was not worth pursuing, the survey by the Associated Press and the NORC Center for Public Affairs Research showed. The findings also indicated declining support for President Donald Trump’s decision to wage war, with few respondents favouring a prolonged conflict. Only two in 10 adults supported continuing US military operations against Iran. Three in 10 said Washington should halt its attacks and pursue another ceasefire through negotiations. The results point to growing public opposition as the war continues to drain US military resources, increase fuel costs, and destabilise the wider Middle East.

items.title: IRGC says it downed hostile drone over southwestern Iran
items.summary: IRGC says it downed hostile drone over southwestern Iran Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says it intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone over the southwestern port city of Bandar Imam Khomeini early on Thursday. The IRGC’s local division detected the unmanned aircraft inside the city’s airspace before shooting it down, the Tasnim news agency reported. Parts of the drone fell onto a residential property following the interception, but authorities reported no deaths. An IRGC explosives team later secured the wreckage, removed it from the house and neutralised any remaining danger, Tasnim said. The military did not identify the drone’s type, origin or intended target. Bandar Imam Khomeini sits on the Gulf coast in Iran’s Khuzestan province and contains one of the country’s most important commercial ports.

Foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Iranian and Omani officials had held several rounds of discussions since talks began last week, including further meetings on Thursday. items.title: Egypt says drone attack sparked fire on American LNG ships
items.summary: Egypt says drone attack sparked fire on American LNG ships Egypt has attributed a fire that damaged two vessels at the Mediterranean port of Damietta to a drone attack, marking its first official account of Wednesday’s incident. The Egyptian cabinet said preliminary findings showed that a drone caused the 29 July blaze. No group has taken responsibility. Authorities have opened an investigation into the circumstances of the attack, citing the need to defend Egypt’s national security and interests. Maritime security company Ambrey said the drone struck a US-owned floating gas storage tanker before flames spread to a second vessel. Officials reported no casualties. Egypt’s Petroleum Ministry had previously confirmed the fire but did not identify its cause. The attack has raised fears that the regional war could spread further after Iran targeted US-linked interests in several countries. If confirmed as part of the wider conflict, it would represent the first attack of its kind on Egyptian territory since the war began.

items.title: Trump's Lebanon fantasy is running smack into reality
items.summary: On June 26, two official delegations — one from Israel and one from Lebanon — signed a framework agreement with great fanfare in Washington. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, openly enthusiastic, framed the event as paving the way toward “lasting peace and security” between Beirut and Tel Aviv. A month later, President Donald Trump received Lebanese President Joseph Aoun at the White House. Once again, Rubio welcomed the visit and reiterated the goal of disarming Hezbollah and achieving a complete and definitive peace between Lebanon and its southern neighbor. Like Tel Aviv, Rubio favors a top-down approach that centers on force and coercion. To neutralize both Tehran and Hezbollah, this camp hopes to combine strong military action against Iranian territory with maximum pressure on the government in Beirut. The goal is two-fold: to strong-arm the Lebanese government into sidelining Hezbollah and to permanently separate the Lebanese and Iranian equations. Within the Trump administration, not everyone is convinced that this roadmap is the most effective approach. Vice President JD Vance

items.title: How much is your support for Israel worth? Try $1 billion.
items.summary: Israel is spending wads of cash on public diplomacy in a desperate attempt to reverse waning American support for the country after it stands accused of genocide in Gaza and pushing the U.S. into the Iran war. items.title: Climate Change Archives - Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
items.summary: In 1978, the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists published a cover story titled “Is mankind warming the Earth?” The answer then, as now, was an “unqualified ‘yes.’” Between July 2023 and June 2024, the average global temperature was over 1.5 degrees Celsius (or 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warmer than the pre-industrial average, the result of over a century of rampant fossil fuel use and associated greenhouse gas emissions. This warming has resulted in global climate change. The Bulletin covers all aspects of the causes and wide-ranging impacts of this existential crisis, from glacier retreat and sea level rise to drought, extreme weather, and intense wildfires. We also investigate the most promising ways to slow and eventually halt global warming, probing uncertainties and irreversible tipping points in the Earth’s climate and biosphere that threatens all life on Earth.

Al-Sadr warned the groups against pulling the country into another conflict and called on Baghdad to assert state control. “Rogue militias must not give our brothers in the Gulf states a pretext to target our sacred land,” he wrote on X. "Above all, Lindsey Graham believed in a strong America," Trump said. "He had unwavering faith in the righteousness of American power." items.summary: As part of its coverage of disruptive technologies that might come to pose global-scale threats, the Bulletin publishes articles on all the ways in which emerging science and technology can affect biological risks. COVID-19 highlighted those risks and led to voluminous coverage of the pandemic and related subjects, including gain-of-function research that could create potentially dangerous new pathogens that might, if accidentally released, spark a disease outbreak. But we also attempt to answer a wide variety of biosecurity- and biosafety-related questions: Are the laboratories used to study pathogens as safe and secure as they need to be? Will artificial intelligence make it easier and simpler for bad actors to develop or use biological weapons? Will efforts at human enhancement spark arms races or exacerbate societal inequality? Do policies that reduce compulsory vaccination increase the threat of diseases once thought tamed? Can political disinformation about bioweapons disrupt international efforts to minimize threats?

items.title: 'Trump Needs a Way Out of This War': Michel Yakovleff explains 'charade' over US-Iran negotiations
items.summary:
Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome General Michel Yakovleff, Professor at Sciences-Po and Former Vice-Chief of Staff at NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe (Shape).. He presents a strategic rather than tactical reading of the current lull in the US-Iran conflict. He argues that the apparent de-escalation is not evidence of diplomatic progress but of mounting structural constraints. Rather than viewing pauses in hostilities as signs of imminent peace, he frames them as consequences of political pressure, military logistics and industrial limitations.
 
At the centre of his argument is the proposition that modern warfare is ultimately governed by sustainability. Missile stockpiles, industrial production capacity, domestic political legitimacy and alliance commitments become as decisive as battlefield success. General Yakovleff contends that the United States retains ample military capability to continue operations against Iran in isolation, yet doing so progressively erodes its ability to deter other adversaries, reassure allies and sustain global commitments.

items.title: Trump is playing chicken with America's oil reserves
items.summary: Back in 1975, reeling from the Arab Oil Embargo of 1973, President Gerald Ford signed the Energy Policy and Conservation Act. The law established the nation’s Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) and framed it as a rainy day fund, made ready for the benefit of the American people should a crisis in supply reach us once more. Today, after two consecutive administrations, our rainy day fund has been drawn down to the lowest levels since 1983 . Biden drew down 50 million barrels in response to COVID. The next year, he withdrew an additional 180 million barrels in response to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, the largest release in SPR history, arguing that the move was needed to calm gasoline prices and cushion the shock from the war. Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration (July 2026) Now, President Donald Trump is draining what is left to manage the price and supply shocks of his Iran war. The poll, conducted Friday through Sunday, also showed the Republican president's approval rating ticking higher to 37 percent, up three points from last month when his rating tied the lowest of his presidency. The poll found that 69 percent of Americans, including four in 10 Republicans, think Trump has not "clearly explained the goals of US military involvement in Iran." Approval of the conflict has been below 40 percent since the US and Israel launched strikes on 28 February - a stark contrast to the opening months of other recent conflicts. While each had different context, the Iraq War from 2003 to 2011 had the support of about 70 percent of Americans in its early months. items.title: Disruptive Technologies Archives - Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
items.summary: The Bulletin’s disruptive technology vertical tracks a wide variety of scientific and technological advances that could—either in the present or the future—pose an existential threat to humanity. These technology areas include biosecurity and biological threats more generally; generative artificial intelligence and its deployment in various industries; autonomous weapons; digitized surveillance systems; and cyber-enabled information warfare that can pollute, and cause chaos in, the world’s information ecosystem. How can humans attempt to roll out new technologies responsibly, benefitting the greater good without destroying civilization in the process? This space is dedicated to answering that question in all its ethical dimensions.

items.title: Nuclear Risk Archives - Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
items.summary: Founded by scientists and engineers of the Manhattan Project in the wake of the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists has been alerting humanity to the danger of nuclear catastrophe since December 1945. For 80 years, the Bulletin has relentlessly pursued this mission by informing the public, policymakers, and scientists about new and evolving risks from nuclear technologies. Our authors include the world’s leading experts in the fields of nuclear weapons and their delivery platforms, nuclear security, nuclear safety, and nuclear waste policy. These experts and a staff of editors work together to provide accessible, authoritative articles for policy makers and citizens alike, with the aim of ensuring that nuclear science makes life on Earth better, not worse.

Beijing accused him of spying. The Tatmadaw, or military, seized power in 1962 and has ruled the country in varying iterations ever since. items.title: Zelensky's 'Freya' missile defense scheme could backfire. Here's why.
items.summary: According to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, neutralizing Russia’s ballistic missile threat is a key to ending the war that continues to ravage his country. “This is Russia’s last major advantage,” he told fellow leaders at the NATO summit earlier this month. Kyiv’s ability to achieve this goal today is limited. So far this year, Russia has launched over 500 ballistic missiles at Ukraine. In June 2026, these attacks contributed to almost 300 Ukrainian civilian deaths. U.S.-made Patriot interceptors are the only reliable defense against Russia’s ballistic missile attacks, but these are in short supply, especially since the war in Iran forced Washington to divert much of its existing stockpile to the Middle East. Zelensky’s answer to this challenge is the Freya , a Ukrainian-developed air defense system he hopes will give the country its own anti-ballistic missile protection while also integrating the country irreversibly with European partners. From the strait of Hormuz to the North Sea, a global maritime war rages around us – and more than the price of oil is at stake | Simon Tisdall
items.summary: The collapse of the rules-based order is not confined to the land: we’re imperilled as centuries of maritime cooperation sink beneath the waves The US military campaign to protect merchant shipping from Iranian attacks by asserting direct maritime control in the strait of Hormuz is not an idea unique to Donald Trump’s administration. Almost exactly 200 years ago, in the period 1825-27, a powerful US naval squadron led by Commodore John Rodgers was sent to the Mediterranean to defend American ships from the depredations of Greek corsairs and pirates. For all the new-minted republic’s brave talk of liberty, the US squadron did not assist Greece’s ongoing “regime change” struggle for independence from the Ottoman empire. Its sole, self-serving purpose was to defend US trade, markets and business interests. After abandoning his call for a people’s revolution in Tehran , this, too, is what Trump’s reckless war with Iran has now boiled down to. Simon Tisdall is a Guardian foreign affairs commentator Continue reading...

Trump vloog daarheen met de Boeing 747-8 die hij van de regering van Qatar cadeau had gekregen. De Amerikaanse veiligheidsdienst Secret Service drong er volgens de NYT bij Trump op aan om van toestel te wisselen. Dat zou gebeuren uit "veiligheidsoverwegingen". Het luxe regeringsvliegtuig heeft minder geavanceerde veiligheidssystemen dan de twee oudere Air Force One-toestellen. Zo mist het toestel cruciale verdedigingssystemen, zoals anti-raketapparatuur. De schending van het luchtruim werd om 08.22 uur opgemerkt, waarna twee F-16's werden ingezet. Het ministerie heeft niet bekendgemaakt waar de drone vandaan kwam. Het is voor het eerst dat Roemenië zelf actief onbemande toestellen neerhaalt. items.title: Vuurbal te zien boven delen van Nederland: 'Best een lichtspektakel'
items.summary: In delen van Nederland was rond 22.30 uur een vuurbal aan de hemel te zien. Onder meer vanuit Amsterdam, Utrecht, Almere, Dronten, Arnhem en het Friese Gaastmeer kwamen berichten van mensen die het bijzondere fenomeen in de avondschemering zagen. Volgens satellietdeskundige Marco Langbroek van de TU Delft gaat het om een satelliet van Elon Musks SpaceX die terugkeerde in de atmosfeer, Starlink 1541. "Hij kwam boven Engeland de atmosfeer binnen en begon daar op te breken en op te branden. Dat gebeurt doorgaans op hoogtes tussen de 90 en 50 kilometer." items.summary: Nederland is begonnen met het op de markt brengen van een deel van de strategische oliereserve. Dat moet de omhooggeschoten olieprijs drukken. Het gaat om 2,7 miljoen vaten van commerciële partijen. De komende weken volgt mogelijk ook een deel van de voorraad van de Staat. In maart kondigde het Internationaal Energieagentschap (IEA) aan 400 miljoen vaten uit de noodreserves van de aangesloten landen vrij te geven. Tot nu toe waren de Nederlandse reserves niet nodig, maar door de oplopende olieprijs is er nu wel behoefte aan. Lidstaten zijn verplicht een oliereserve aan te houden die gelijkstaat aan circa drie maanden aan import. Mede daardoor steeg de olieprijs vandaag verder naar meer dan 100 dollar per vat. Waarom mengen de Houthi's zich juist nu in het conflict? De antwoorden op vijf vragen over de Houthi's. Wie zijn de Houthi's? Jemeniet Hussein al-Houthi richtte in 1992 de Houthi's op als vreedzame verzetsbeweging in het noorden van Jemen. Ze horen bij de zaidieten, een sjiitische moslimminderheid in het land. De officiële naam van de beweging is ' Ansar Allah ', wat 'aanhangers van God' betekent. Ze zijn het niet eens met hoe Jemen geregeerd wordt en vinden dat de regering hun woongebied in het noorden verwaarloost. In 2011 rukten de Houthi's op en namen de Jemenitische hoofdstad Sanaa in, met een burgeroorlog tot gevolg. De officiële en internationaal erkende regering huisvest zich in de zuidelijke havenstad Aden. The vote was 214-208 in favour of the war powers resolution as four Republicans joined Democrats in voting for it. The resolution, introduced by Representative Pramila Jayapal, a Washington Democrat, directs Trump "to remove the use of United States Armed Forces from hostilities" against Iran unless Congress authorises it. However, it was largely symbolic. Lawmakers have passed similar resolutions repeatedly in recent months, but they have not led to the cessation of war.

items.title: Iran crisis is not solely a product of Trump’s rule | Letters
items.summary: Focusing on Donald Trump’s defects risks making war appear as an aberration rather than as a recurring feature of American power, writes David Eaton . Plus letters from Blaine Stothard and Harvey Gilbert Simon Tisdall’s article ( Trump, not Iran, is the world’s greatest danger. He’s a one-man weapon of mass destruction, 18 July ) is a forceful polemic, but it risks turning a structural problem into a personal one. If Donald Trump is uniquely reckless, that deserves criticism. Yet the article implies that America’s present predicament is chiefly the consequence of his character, rather than asking why successive administrations, Republican and Democrat alike, have repeatedly resorted to military intervention in the Middle East. To focus on Trump’s defects risks making war itself appear as an aberration rather than as a recurring feature of American power. The same applies to the strait of Hormuz. Gulf states and their allies are now racing to build rival lines. The fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act, or NDAA, authorises an unprecedented $1.15 trillion in military spending and passed the House by a vote of 216 to 212. The vote was largely along party lines, as all but seven Republicans voted in favour of the measure and all but six Democrats voted against. The NDAA has come under fire for a provision aimed at increasing military technology cooperation with Israel, despite growing support among voters for halting military assistance to Israel. The bill's future in the Senate is now uncertain as Democrats objected to the substantial funding allocated to the Pentagon at a time when President Donald Trump and his fellow Republicans are slashing spending on social programmes. De blokkade heeft betrekking op het verkeer door de zeestraat Bab el-Mandeb, tussen Jemen en de Hoorn van Afrika. De zeestraat is net als de Straat van Hormuz belangrijk voor de olie-export en dreigt een nieuw brandpunt te worden in het conflict in de regio. Het is nog onduidelijk welke gevolgen de aangekondigde maritieme blokkade heeft voor de internationale scheepvaart in het gebied. Tijdens de oorlog in Gaza vielen de Houthi's maandenlang schepen aan in en rond de Rode Zee. Gisteren wijzigden vijf tankers hun koers in de Rode Zee om de zeestraat Bab el-Mandeb te mijden.

items.summary: Israel's spy chief held talks on Iran war in Washington, Axios reports The head of Israel's Mossad intelligence agency travelled to Washington two weeks ago to discuss the Iran war, in his first visit to the US capital since taking office, Axios reported on Wednesday, citing two unidentified sources with knowledge of the situation. He met with CIA director John Ratcliffe and White House officials, the report said.

items.title: Iran's Ghalibaf says no one will sell oil in the region if Iran cannot
items.summary: Iran's Ghalibaf says no one will sell oil in the region if Iran cannot Iran's top negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said on Wednesday that no one will be able to sell oil in a region where Iran is not able to do so, adding that if Tehran's security is not ensured, no infrastructure will be safe. items.title: Iraanse fotograaf laat zien dat 'Hormuz' meer is dan oorlog
items.summary: Al bijna twee weken worden de bombardementen op Iran alsmaar heviger. Niet alleen militaire doelen, ook doelen die burgers gebruiken worden steeds meer geraakt. Zo zijn rondom de zuidelijke havenstad Bandar Abbas tunnels, bruggen en communicatie-infrastructuur gebombardeerd. Dat heeft natuurlijk impact op de bevolking. Want waar de oorlog en de Straat van Hormuz voor veel mensen een nieuwskop zijn, is het gebied ook een thuis voor miljoenen Iraniërs. De Iraanse fotograaf Morteza Niknahad (42) portretteert al jaren de mensen uit zijn omgeving. Hij geeft met zijn werk een uniek inkijkje in het leven van de inwoners van het gebied die we nauwelijks te horen of te zien krijgen. "Het geluid van explosies is er constant. We blijven hele nachten wakker om het nieuws te volgen", vertelt Niknahad in een spraakbericht. De fotograaf, geboren en getogen in de zuidelijke havenstad Bandar Abbas, maakt al jaren foto's van het gebied rond de Straat van Hormuz.
